correctness.rationale: All definitions and quantifiers are explicit. For <=4 vertices, residual graphs are totally ordered by edge-addition up to relabeling, giving a common stochastically minimal deletion for all p. For exactly five vertices, standalone exact checker enumerates all 2^10 labeled graphs and 5! permutations to form 21 connected classes, proves global polynomial sign inequalities by rational Sturm root isolation, and checks all 105 vertex-deletion objective polynomials using a second induced-component decomposition. Exactly two classes have disjoint optima iff 1/4<p<3/4, with exact rational factors and strict exclusion of other vertices. Finite exhaustive proof is used only for its bounded five-vertex domain, not as a claim for arbitrary n.

originality.rationale: The new assertion is a complete two-objective finite classification: among the 21 connected five-vertex graph types, exactly two have incompatible mean and three-case-tail optimal vaccination sites, and only for 1/4<p<3/4; graphs of order at most four admit a common optimum. Existing full-text sources use different transmission laws, larger structured populations, different objectives, or only expected case counts. An earlier exact mean-only theorem on one witness graph is acknowledged; it does not establish the distinct tail preference or all-class classification. Exact root-sign and two-method polynomial verification provide independent mathematical support for the new comparisons, though literature completeness is not provable.

value.rationale: Mean infection count and probability of at least three infections are naturally distinct prophylactic objectives; no arbitrary parameter slice was introduced. The exact earliest conflict order, complete enumeration of exceptional connected graph types, and the common conflict interval offer a reusable small-network benchmark separating risk-neutral from harm-threshold interventions. Does not claim clinical value or population-scale generalization.
